title: Open WebUI chat completions -- T1005 image_url resolved as a foreign file id, exfiltrated via LLM OCR
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54009 (GHSA-wch8-mhj5-9frg,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

`POST /api/chat/completions` accepts an `image_url.url` value that,
when it does NOT start with `http://`, `https://`, or `data:image/`,
is interpreted as a raw FILE ID and resolved against the global file
table -- with NO OWNERSHIP CHECK. An authenticated user can set
`image_url.url` to another user's file id; the server reads that
file from disk, base64-encodes it, and injects it into the LLM
request as if it were a legitimately-supplied image. The attacker
then simply prompts the model to describe or OCR the "image" and
reads the victim's private file content back through the model's own
response -- an indirect, LLM-mediated exfiltration channel for a file
the attacker never had legitimate access to.

Detection logic flags a chat-completions request whose `image_url.url`
field is a bare identifier (matching a file-id shape rather than an
`http(s)://` or `data:image/` URI) that does not belong to the
requesting user -- the exact ambiguity the vulnerable code exploited
by treating "not a URL" as "must be my own file id".

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6.
